speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned presenting with a breast mass; how long have you noticed this lump, and has its size or consistency changed recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 48-year-old woman. The patient noticed a mass in her left breast 4 weeks ago, which has rapidly increased in size. She denies any recent trauma or infections. No history of similar complaints in the past.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given the rapid growth over 4 weeks, have you experienced any pain, skin changes like dimpling or redness, or nipple discharge? Also, do you notice any enlarged lumps in your armpit?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Presence of a left breast mass. I also have Rapid increase in size of the mass, No skin or nipple changes, No pain associated with the mass.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Phyllodes Tumor

The rapid increase in size over just four weeks is highly characteristic of a Phyllodes tumor, which often grows faster than a typical fibroadenoma. Since you have no skin changes, nipple discharge, or pain, this points away from inflammatory conditions or advanced carcinoma, but we need confirmation. I would like to see the imaging and pathology to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST IMAGES: Mammogram_and_Ultrasound.
